source.title: Modularity in Transformers: Investigating Neuron Separability & Specialization
source.authors: Nicholas Pochinkov; T. Jones; Mohammed Rashidur Rahman

record.tranche_reason: The paper analyzes task-specific neuron importance and clustering, but does not measure whether individual neurons respond strongly to unrelated inputs. Its overlap and cluster results concern a related construct, not the polysemanticity named by the claim versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports selected-neuron overlap across task or data subsets and correspondence between selected neurons and MoEfication clusters. These are findings about task-specific neuron importance and grouping, not direct measurements of neurons responding to multiple unrelated inputs. The paper also cites prior work on neurons potentially representing multiple features; those cited results are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study measures overlap of neuron sets selected as important for class or data subsets (via selective pruning) and their correspondence with MoEfication clusters. It never measures whether individual neurons respond to several unrelated inputs, so no version is tested. Polysemanticity appears only as cited background (Elhage et al. 2022, Pona 2023). Set overlap between, say, dissimilar Cifar20 classes could hint at neurons shared across unrelated classes. But the authors don't analyze individual neurons or frame overlap as polysemanticity, and random-init models show similar overlap patterns.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors also frame the random-versus-trained overlap as evidence for a weak Lottery Ticket Hypothesis. They note that cross-class pruning effects show shared pathways between related classes.
record.recipe_differences: Uses selective-pruning importance scores and balanced k-means MoEfication clustering to analyze task specialization and neuron-set overlap; it does not apply the original neuron-visualization or SoLU methods.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported MoEfication-to-task-neuron correspondence varies by layer: stronger in earlier ViT layers, and stronger in earlier and later Mistral layers than in middle layers.

fits_no_version.finding: Selected-neuron sets for different Cifar20 classes and text subsets overlap. Overlap patterns are broadly similar between trained and randomly initialized models, and training shrinks extreme overlaps between dissimilar classes.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Neuron sets important for different data subsets overlap, more for related subsets, and partly reflect structure present at initialization.

fits_no_version.finding: Task-selected neurons concentrate in MoEfication clusters more than in random models. Correspondence is strongest in early ViT layers, and in early and late Mistral layers.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Co-activation clusters align with task-specific neurons more in layers near input or output than in middle layers.

fits_no_version.finding: Selectively pruning neurons for one class lowers accuracy on related classes (Figures 1-2), with asymmetric cross-effects. No row records this.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Pruning neurons important for one task degrades related tasks, indicating shared neural pathways.

record.problems: The paper says its specialization interpretation is somewhat qualitative and would benefit from more rigorous statistical analysis. It studies only selected tasks and datasets, excludes attention mechanisms, and reports the overlap and layer correspondence figures without numerical values in the text.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant reported results left out.

untested.parts: No per-neuron response analysis in vision models (ViT studied only through task-importance sets).
No measure of the share of MLP neurons responding to unrelated tokens or contexts, by layer or otherwise.
No test of superposition as the cause.
The random-init comparison concerns importance-set overlap, not polysemanticity under ample capacity.
No architecture, activation-function or regularization comparison.
No reinspection of canonical polysemantic neurons.
No comparison of activation ranges or explanation scoring.

record.verdict_notes: No verdicts are given because no version is tested. The unrecorded pruning cross-effect results (Section 3, Figures 1-2) are relevant only to the fits_no_version construct, not to any version.

versions.untested_parts: No direct measurement of individual neuron responses to multiple image classes or unrelated image inputs.
No direct measurement of individual MLP neuron responses across unrelated tokens or contexts, or of the share of such neurons by layer.
Does not test whether polysemanticity is caused by representing more sparse features than there are neurons.
Although it compares trained and randomly initialized models, it does not measure polysemanticity or test its occurrence without capacity pressure.
Does not compare activation functions or architectures for polysemanticity, or test whether its share can be lowered without a large performance loss.
Does not inspect canonical polysemantic neurons to determine whether their inputs share a feature or job.
Does not compare activation ranges or explanation-scoring methods for their effect on polysemanticity.

rows.subject: ViT-Base-224
rows.operation_detail: Compared overlap of neurons selected as important for Cifar20 classes in trained and randomly initialized models.
rows.measure: Intersection of selected-neuron sets between classes
rows.note: The text says trained and random models have broadly similar overlap patterns but different magnitudes; trained selections show diminished extreme overlaps and larger overlaps for some intuitively similar classes. This measures task-importance overlap, not polysemantic responses.

rows.subject: Mistral 7B instruct v0.2
rows.operation_detail: Compared overlap of neurons selected as important for text subsets in trained and randomly initialized models.

conditions.value: Pile subsets and additional specialized datasets

rows.measure: Intersection of selected-neuron sets between text subsets
rows.note: The text says the overall overlap patterns are analogous to ViT; most extreme overlaps diminish, while some intuitively similar subsets retain or gain overlap. This measures task-importance overlap, not individual neuron responses across contexts.
rows.check: The condition says top 3.4 ± 2.6% of neurons, but the Figure 4 caption says the top 1% for Mistral. The text is inconsistent; note both.

rows.subject: ViT-Base-224
rows.operation_detail: Compared sorted overlap values for class-specific selected neurons between trained and randomly initialized models.
rows.measure: Distribution and correlation of class-pair selected-neuron overlaps
rows.note: The text reports a definite correlation between trained and random overlaps, with large shifts, and says ViT overlaps are more tightly bound. This is not a direct polysemanticity measure.

rows.subject: Mistral 7B instruct v0.2
rows.operation_detail: Compared sorted overlap values for text-subset selected neurons between trained and randomly initialized models.
rows.measure: Distribution and correlation of text-subset selected-neuron overlaps
rows.note: The text reports a definite correlation between trained and random overlaps, large shifts, and overall lower overlaps in Mistral. This is not a direct polysemanticity measure.

rows.subject: ViT-Base-224
rows.operation_detail: Measured how selected neurons are distributed among MoEfication clusters by layer.
rows.measure: Correspondence of selected neurons with MoEfication clusters
rows.note: The text says trained selected neurons correspond relatively strongly with clusters compared with random selections, with stronger correspondence in earlier layers. The measure concerns clustering, not polysemanticity.

rows.subject: Mistral 7B instruct v0.2
rows.operation_detail: Measured how selected neurons are distributed among MoEfication clusters by layer.

conditions.value: earlier and later layers versus middle layers

rows.measure: Correspondence of selected neurons with MoEfication clusters
rows.note: The text says trained selected neurons correspond more with clusters and that correspondence is stronger in earlier and later layers than in middle layers. The measure concerns clustering, not polysemanticity.
